# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 68

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 9

---

## Disagreement 1 — 68:1 "He cannot" vs. "He is unable"

- **EMET:** "He cannot keep them away"
- **LOGOS:** "He is unable to keep them away"
- **PNEUMA:** "He can't protect them from it"
- **Greek:** *ou dynastai* — is not able
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "He is unable to keep them away" (LOGOS). "Is unable" is more formal than "cannot"; PNEUMA's "protect them from it" substitutes "protect" for the specific "keep away."

---

## Disagreement 2 — 68:1 "appointed these torments for the testing" vs. "appointed these afflictions for the testing"

- **EMET:** "appointed these torments for the testing"
- **LOGOS:** "appointed these afflictions for the testing"
- **PNEUMA:** "appointed these afflictions to test"
- **Greek:** *etas basanous...eis peirasmon* — these torments/afflictions for testing
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "appointed these afflictions for the testing" (LOGOS). "Afflictions" is slightly less severe than "torments" in this general context; both are valid.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 68:2 "not all can endure equally" vs. "not all are equally able to endure"

- **EMET:** "not all can endure equally"
- **LOGOS:** "not all are equally able to endure"
- **PNEUMA:** "not everyone is equally capable of enduring"
- **Greek:** *ou pantes dynantai hypomonein* — not all are able to endure
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "not all are equally able to endure" (LOGOS). The "equally" is implicit in the context; LOGOS's phrasing is most natural.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 68:2 "perfected" vs. "brought to full maturity"

- **EMET:** "that they may be perfected"
- **LOGOS:** "so that they may be perfected"
- **PNEUMA:** "so that they can be brought to full maturity"
- **Greek:** *teleōthōsin* — that they may be completed/perfected
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "so that they may be perfected" (LOGOS). *Teleioō* = to complete/perfect; "perfected" is the standard translation; PNEUMA's "maturity" is interpretively accurate but less precise.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 68:2 "not completely broken" vs. "not completely overwhelmed"

- **EMET:** "they may not be completely broken"
- **LOGOS:** "that they may not be completely overwhelmed"
- **PNEUMA:** "so they aren't completely crushed"
- **Greek:** *mē apōlōntai holōs* — that they may not perish entirely
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "that they may not be completely overwhelmed" (LOGOS). "Overwhelmed" captures the crushing weight without implying permanent destruction; "completely broken" (EMET) suggests fracture; PNEUMA's "crushed" is too physical.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 68:3 "give back his wage" vs. "repay his wage"

- **EMET:** "give back to each one his wage"
- **LOGOS:** "repay to each person his wage"
- **PNEUMA:** "pay each person back according to what they have done"
- **Greek:** *apodōsei hekastō ton misthon* — will give back to each one the wage
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "repay to each person his wage" (LOGOS). "Repay" has the sense of a debt being settled; "wage" (*misthos*) should be preserved; PNEUMA loses "wage."

---

## Disagreement 7 — 68:3 "after a long time" vs. "after the full time has passed"

- **EMET:** "after a long time the Lord will give back"
- **LOGOS:** "after the full time has passed, the Lord will repay"
- **PNEUMA:** "after the full time has passed"
- **Greek:** *meta chronon apodōsei* — after the time/after time has passed
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "after the full time has passed" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). "The full time" implies there is an appointed duration; EMET's "long time" is less specific.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 68:4 "not overcome by them" vs. "not broken in mind"

- **EMET:** "not overcome by them...not broken in mind"
- **LOGOS:** "not overcome by them...mind is not broken"
- **PNEUMA:** "without being overcome...without their spirit being broken"
- **Greek:** *mē kratoumenas...mē suntriphōsin tēi dianoia* — not mastered...not shattered in mind/understanding
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "not overcome by them...not broken in mind" (EMET/LOGOS). The *dianoia* (mind/understanding) is the locus; PNEUMA's "spirit" changes the anthropological term.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 68:4 "grow great in it" — the life

- **EMET:** "receives life and grows great in it"
- **LOGOS:** "shall receive life and grow great in it"
- **PNEUMA:** "will receive life and grow great in it"
- **Note:** All three agree on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "shall receive life and grow great in it" (LOGOS). The future promise is appropriately expressed with "shall."

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 68.*
